citation: Ramel-Delobel 2024, Air pollution exposure in active versus passive travel modes meta-analysis

citation: Zhang 2017, Comparison of PM2.5 exposure in hazy and non-hazy days in Nanjing

citation: Zhang 2017, Comparison of PM2.5 exposure in hazy and non-hazy days in Nanjing

citation: Schlunssen 2023, Prevalences and levels of occupational exposure to silica asbestos and coal, WHO/ILO Joint Estimates

citation: Schlunssen 2023, Prevalences and levels of occupational exposure to silica asbestos and coal, WHO/ILO Joint Estimates
evidence: For the construction sector the pooled prevalence of occupational silica exposure was 0.89 and of asbestos exposure 0.77, the largest bodies of evidence were construction, manufacturing and mining.

citation: Boadu 2023, Work-related respiratory health conditions among construction workers systematic review
evidence: 25 studies identified 16 respiratory conditions in construction workers, cough, dyspnoea and asthma the top three, with dust, respirable crystalline silica, fumes, vapours, asbestos and gases as the hazards, and extended exposure time increasing risk.

citation: Bello 2019, Occupational exposures to respirable silica and dust in demolition crushing and chipping

citation: Bello 2019, Occupational exposures to respirable silica and dust in demolition crushing and chipping
evidence: Perimeter area samples (n=33) were collected to assess potential bystanders' exposures and showed bystanders at crushing sites could be exposed to higher levels than at demolition sites.

citation: Bello 2019, Occupational exposures to respirable silica and dust in demolition crushing and chipping
evidence: Crushing tender exposures fell below the OSHA PEL of 50 ug/m3 when the crusher's water spraying system was used but not with a water cannon, chipping workers stayed above the PEL even with N95 respirators.

citation: Pradhan 2019, Heat stress impacts on cardiac mortality in Nepali migrant workers in Qatar

citation: Pradhan 2019, Heat stress impacts on cardiac mortality in Nepali migrant workers in Qatar

citation: Kang 2021, Real-time automated monitoring system for hazardous pollutants at the construction site
evidence: Management of dust from construction sites is essential to minimise the health damage of nearby residents, motivating real-time perimeter monitoring.

citation: HEI 2022, Special Report 23 Long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution executive summary

citation: HEI 2022, Special Report 23 Long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution executive summary

citation: HEI 2022, Special Report 23 Long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution executive summary

citation: HEI 2022, Special Report 23 Long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution executive summary

citation: HEI 2022, Special Report 23 Long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution executive summary

citation: HEI 2022, Special Report 23 Long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution executive summary

citation: HEI 2022, Special Report 23 Long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution executive summary
evidence: Moderate confidence for term low birth weight, RR 1.11 (1.03 to 1.20) per 5 ug/m3 PM2.5, and small for gestational age 1.09 (1.04 to 1.14), preterm birth largely null.

citation: Tjoe Nij 2003, Dust control measures in the construction industry
evidence: Short-term measurements showed reduction factors above 70 percent when wet dust suppression or local exhaust ventilation was used, while full-shift respirable quartz reached 63 times the MAC and more than half of measurements exceeded it.

citation: Rappaport 2003, Excessive exposure to silica in the US construction industry
evidence: Probability of overexposure above the 0.05 mg/m3 silica OEL was 64.5 to 100 percent across bricklayers, painters, operating engineers and laborers at 36 sites, wet suppression cut laborer silica exposure about 3 fold and ventilated cabs about 6 fold.

citation: Chang 2010, Fugitive dust source profiles and control strategies at gravel processing sites in Taiwan
evidence: PM10 at the site boundary ranged 135 to 550 ug/m3, wet suppression on paved roads gave 50 to 83 percent control efficiency, surfactant spraying on unpaved roads about 93 percent, revegetation 48 to 64 percent.

citation: Chang 2010, Fugitive dust source profiles and control strategies at gravel processing sites in Taiwan
evidence: Fugitive dust from piles, unpaved roads, crushers and bare ground produced boundary TSP of 280 to 1290 ug/m3 and PM10 of 135 to 550 ug/m3, above the 125 ug/m3 daily standard.

citation: Middaugh 2012, Cut-off saw exposure control methods for respirable dust and silica in roadway construction
evidence: Wet suppression cut respirable dust from 16.4 to 3.60 mg/m3 (78 percent) and local exhaust to 4.40 mg/m3 (73 percent) during curb cutting, yet workers still exceed the quartz TLV within an hour.

citation: Ham 2024, Particulate matter reduction efficiency of sprinkler system as targeted control for construction activity
evidence: In a 4 m by 4 m dust chamber a targeted sprinkler cut PM10 by 95 percent with water at 115 bar and 83 percent at 100 bar, dust suppressant peaked at 83 percent at 100 bar.

citation: Choi 2023, Effect of dust barriers on PM dispersion from a construction site using CFD
evidence: CFD under four wind directions showed PM exposure of residents next to a construction site varies by up to 2.3 times with wind direction.

citation: Choi 2023, Effect of dust barriers on PM dispersion from a construction site using CFD
evidence: Optimal dust barrier heights determined by CFD reduced resident PM exposure and a flexible height approach was effective in all four wind directions.

citation: Choi 2023, Effect of dust barriers on PM dispersion from a construction site using CFD
evidence: Resident exposure depended on wind direction by up to 2.3 times, so control aimed at the downwind side addresses the dominant exposure condition (mechanism only).

citation: Kim 2021, IoT-based particulate matter monitoring system for construction sites
evidence: PM generated on construction sites poses serious health risks to field workers and residents living near construction sites and must be managed in real time at multiple locations.

citation: Kim 2025, Automated human-centric construction dust alert system field test
evidence: Over 153 days at a Korean site 55 events above 35.5 ug/m3 PM2.5 were logged at four nodes, 8 of 24 workers were exposed, peak 842 ug/m3 during floor sweeping.

citation: Kim 2025, Automated human-centric construction dust alert system field test
evidence: Sensor nodes triggered SMS alerts to workers within 20 m when PM2.5 reached 35.5 ug/m3, alerts fired during site preparation, earthwork and indoor work.

citation: Zhou 2007, Factors influencing the spatial extent of mobile source air pollution impacts meta-analysis
evidence: The spatial extent of mobile source impact is 100 to 400 m for EC or PM mass, 200 to 500 m for NO2 and 100 to 300 m for ultrafine particle counts, generally within a few hundred metres of highway or city roads.

citation: Zhou 2007, Factors influencing the spatial extent of mobile source air pollution impacts meta-analysis
evidence: Policymakers can develop reasonable estimates of the zone of influence of mobile sources, on the order of 100 to 500 m depending on pollutant, which is the distance a setback rule has to clear.

citation: Zhou 2007, Factors influencing the spatial extent of mobile source air pollution impacts meta-analysis
evidence: Near-road gradients excluding background extend 100 to 400 m for PM mass and 200 to 500 m for NO2, inert pollutants with high background show no gradient.

citation: Abhijith 2017, Air pollution abatement performances of green infrastructure in open road and street canyon environments review
evidence: For open road conditions wide, low porosity and tall vegetation barriers lead to downwind pollutant reductions, while gaps and high porosity vegetation give no improvement or worse air quality, in street canyons hedges improve and tree canopies worsen air quality.

citation: Abhijith 2017, Air pollution abatement performances of green infrastructure in open road and street canyon environments review
evidence: Studies of personal exposure to local sources under vegetation in open road settings show downwind reductions behind wide, dense, tall barriers, and green walls and roofs are also effective abatement measures.

citation: Nahar 2020, Exposure assessment of emissions from mobile food carts on New York City streets
evidence: Concentrations measured in the micro-environment around carts were highest near charcoal carts, 196 ug/m3 PM2.5 mean and 1520 ug/m3 peak.

citation: Nahar 2020, Exposure assessment of emissions from mobile food carts on New York City streets
evidence: Pollution emission impact ranked charcoal above propane plus charcoal above propane carts, so the fuel used determines the emission and the authors ask policy to regulate by fuel.

citation: Nahar 2020, Exposure assessment of emissions from mobile food carts on New York City streets
evidence: The study measured the air pollution the public is exposed to in the micro-environment around food carts on city streets.

evidence: 50.7 percent of 67 cooking vendors reported respiratory symptoms against 33.3 percent of 18 non-cooking vendors, charcoal users about twice as likely to report cough as LPG users, more than 10 years of tenure about three times the cough odds.

citation: Abdul Wahid 2014, Respiratory symptoms of vendors in an open-air hawker centre in Brunei
evidence: Vendors cooking with charcoal were about two times more likely to have cough than those cooking with LPG.

citation: Kong 2021, Particulate matter concentrations according to cooking activity in a residential environment
evidence: Roasting mackerel with no ventilation reached 1228 ug/m3 PM10 and 761 ug/m3 PM2.5, natural ventilation combined with ventilation devices was the most effective reduction method (residential evidence, mechanism transfer to stalls).

citation: Chu 2021, Air pollution as a determinant of food delivery and related plastic waste
evidence: Among office workers in three Chinese cities a 100 ug/m3 rise in PM2.5 raised the propensity to order food delivery by two fifths of the sample mean, platform data confirmed a smaller causal link.

citation: Li 2025, Carbon monoxide exposure in food delivery workers using exhaled air
evidence: 156 food delivery workers had mean exhaled CO of 4.79 ppm against 1.51 ppm in 49 referents, and among non-smokers 1.57 versus 1.13 ppm (p=0.002), indicating higher traffic CO exposure.

citation: Lawin 2016, Occupational air pollution exposure and respiratory health in motorcycle taxi driving
evidence: 85 motorcycle taxi drivers in Cotonou carried CO loggers 8 h per day and had higher mean CO than matched controls, 7.6 versus 5.4 ppm (p=0.001).

citation: Lawin 2018, Motorcycle taxi drivers' respiratory health against the CO ambient standard, Benin
evidence: Drivers with 8 h CO above 9 ppm had a significantly lower PEF (minus 10 percent, p=0.02) and non-significantly more symptoms (OR 1.67, 95 percent CI 0.26 to 10.74) than less exposed drivers.

citation: Agudelo-Londono 2024, Environmental injustice in air quality for digital platform delivery workers in Bogota
evidence: PM10 and PM2.5 on 56 delivery routes were higher in the lower income locality Kennedy than in Usaquen, linking route geography and road infrastructure to rider exposure.

citation: Alahmad 2023, Extreme heat and work injuries in Kuwait's hot summers
evidence: During the summer midday ban a 39.4 C day raised the relative risk of occupational injury to 1.44 (1.34 to 1.53) versus 37.0 C, and 40 C gave 1.48, despite the calendar based ban.

citation: Alahmad 2023, Extreme heat and work injuries in Kuwait's hot summers
evidence: Calendar based midday work bans may be inadequate for occupational heat protection, especially for migrant workers, injury risk stayed elevated on hot days within the ban period.

citation: Li 2025, Carbon monoxide exposure in food delivery workers using exhaled air
evidence: The number of food delivery workers in online food delivery services has soared recently and they are exposed to air pollutants from traffic exhaust frequently.

citation: Gulf News 2026, UAE summer work ban and 12000 rest stations for delivery riders
evidence: Over 12000 air-conditioned rest areas operate from June 15 to September 15 and riders may choose not to work in the 12:30 to 15:00 restricted period, coordinated with the employer, fourth consecutive year.

evidence: Extremely hot and humid weather on Arabian Gulf construction sites pushed worker heart rate beyond acceptable physiological zones, humidity is named jointly with heat as the exposure.
